legacyQuestion.stem: A respiratory therapist walks with a patient while tracking saturation and activity tolerance. What is the purpose of this evaluation?
legacyQuestion.why: The six-minute walk assessment helps characterize exercise tolerance and oxygen needs.

legacyQuestion.stem: A confused patient repeatedly tries to pull at a line. What is the guiding principle before restraints?
legacyQuestion.why: Restraints are a last resort after appropriate alternatives.
options: Try appropriate less-restrictive alternatives and assess the cause
Skip assessment if the patient is restless

legacyQuestion.stem: A patient lives alone and uses oxygen at home. Which discharge question best identifies a safety concern?
legacyQuestion.why: Home safety assessment should identify oxygen-related ignition risks.
options: “Does anyone smoke or use open flames where oxygen is stored?”

legacyQuestion.stem: An ICU patient becomes agitated when alarms sound and several staff members speak simultaneously. Which initial change is most appropriate?
legacyQuestion.why: Reducing excessive stimuli addresses sensory overload.
options: Reduce unnecessary noise and coordinate communication
Keep the lights bright all night
Increase the number of simultaneous conversations

legacyQuestion.stem: A patient asks to try relaxation before a dressing change. Which actions may support comfort without replacing indicated analgesia? Select all that apply.
legacyQuestion.why: Breathing, imagery, and environment are complementary comfort interventions.
options: Cancel ordered pain medication without discussion

legacyQuestion.stem: A tornado warning is announced. A bedbound patient is near a window. Which action follows the course guidance?
legacyQuestion.why: Tornado precautions prioritize interior protection and distance from windows.
options: Move the bed away from windows and protect the patient as directed
Raise the window shade to watch the storm
Take the patient to an open balcony

legacyQuestion.stem: A COPD patient has a prescription for an inhaled bronchodilator. Which finding best indicates therapeutic benefit?
legacyQuestion.why: Improved airflow and reduced dyspnea suggest bronchodilator benefit.

legacyQuestion.stem: An order is to infuse 600 mL over 5 hours using tubing calibrated at 15 gtt/mL. What is the drip rate to the nearest whole drop?
A patient describes sharp pain directly over a fresh incision that increases when the area is touched. How should the nurse document the location pattern?
legacyQuestion.why: Pain centered at the injured site is localized rather than referred.

legacyQuestion.stem: Match each safety term to its description.
legacyQuestion.why: The course differentiates near misses, patient safety events, sentinel events, and never events.
pairs: Unexpected death or serious harm event
Serious preventable event on a designated list
matchOptions: Unexpected death or serious harm event
Serious preventable event on a designated list

legacyQuestion.stem: A patient received an opioid 20 minutes ago and is difficult to arouse with slow respirations. What is the priority?
legacyQuestion.why: Respiratory depression and reduced responsiveness require immediate assessment and escalation.
options: Assess airway and breathing and activate the appropriate urgent response
Wait until the next pain assessment
Give another opioid for persistent pain

legacyQuestion.stem: A child has an order for 80 mg of an oral liquid. The bottle reads 40 mg/5 mL. How many mL are required?
A patient receives a medication intended for another patient but has no apparent injury. Which statement is accurate?
legacyQuestion.why: Errors reaching patients warrant assessment and reporting even without evident harm.
options: A patient safety event occurred and should be reported per policy
Nothing happened because injury is absent
It is always a sentinel event
Reporting is unnecessary if the patient is stable

legacyQuestion.stem: A patient says, “I'll use petroleum jelly around my nose while wearing oxygen.” What teaching is needed?
legacyQuestion.why: Avoid petroleum-based products near oxygen equipment.
options: Choose an oxygen-safe water-based product if appropriate
Smoking is safe at low oxygen flow
Open flames do not matter with nasal cannula

legacyQuestion.stem: Which statements demonstrate appropriate patient participation in a pain plan? Select all that apply.
legacyQuestion.why: Reporting changes, functional goals, and adjunct measures support individualized pain care.
options: “I will report new or changing pain.”
“I can tell you what pain level allows me to move.”
“I should let my family press my PCA button.”
“I can ask about nonmedication comfort measures.”

legacyQuestion.stem: The order is 150 mg PO. Liquid medication contains 75 mg per 5 mL. How many mL are required?
A client weighs 54.5 kg. Convert to pounds using 2.2 lb/kg and round to the nearest tenth.
Which practices fit the categories discussed in class? Select all that apply.
legacyQuestion.why: The course distinguishes mind–body, energy, manipulative, and biologically based approaches.

legacyQuestion.stem: A patient with diminished foot sensation reports a new blister but no pain. What should the nurse infer?
legacyQuestion.why: Loss of protective sensation can mask injury.
options: Absence of pain does not exclude tissue injury
The blister is harmless because it is painless
The patient is experiencing sensory overload
Pain medication must be administered before inspection

legacyQuestion.stem: The nurse notices a frayed cord on an infusion pump before use. What should the nurse do?
legacyQuestion.why: Damaged electrical equipment must be removed from use and evaluated.
options: Remove the device from service and report it
Wrap it in tape and continue
Use it only when the floor is dry
Ask the patient to avoid touching it

legacyQuestion.stem: A nurse catches an incorrect medication before it reaches the patient. How should the event be classified?
legacyQuestion.why: An intercepted error that does not reach the patient is a near miss.

legacyQuestion.stem: A patient practices guided imagery before a painful procedure. How should the nurse classify the technique?
legacyQuestion.why: Guided imagery is a mind–body approach.

legacyQuestion.stem: A patient with COPD becomes too short of breath to finish a sentence and appears newly confused. Which action has priority?
legacyQuestion.why: Acute mental-status and respiratory changes may indicate serious deterioration.
options: Prompt respiratory assessment and escalation of care
Encourage the patient to walk alone

legacyQuestion.stem: An order is for 500 mg PO. Tablets are labeled 250 mg each. How many tablets should the nurse give?
legacyQuestion.why: 500 ÷ 250 = 2 tablets.

legacyQuestion.stem: A COPD patient becomes breathless while bathing. What instruction supports energy conservation?
legacyQuestion.why: Pacing and controlled breathing support activity tolerance.
options: Exhale during effort rather than holding breath

legacyQuestion.stem: Before discharge, a patient who uses a walker says the bathroom has loose rugs. Which action is best?
legacyQuestion.why: Home safety planning addresses environment and available support.

legacyQuestion.stem: A patient is breathing rapidly during severe anxiety and reports tingling fingers. Which change is most consistent with hyperventilation?
legacyQuestion.why: Hyperventilation increases CO₂ exhalation and may lower arterial CO₂.

legacyQuestion.stem: An active shooter is nearby and no safe exit is available. What should staff do according to the course guidance?
legacyQuestion.why: Hide and secure the location when evacuation is unsafe.
options: Hide out of sight, lock or barricade, and silence phones
Call out loudly to locate others
Leave the door open for visibility

legacyQuestion.stem: Which findings suggest a sensory deficit rather than insufficient environmental stimulation? Select all that apply.
legacyQuestion.why: Deficit means impaired reception or processing of sensory input, not simply lack of stimulation.
options: Reduced touch sensation in the toes

legacyQuestion.stem: Match each oxygen-delivery device with its defining clinical use or requirement.
legacyQuestion.why: The oxygen devices differ by flow, concentration control, and design.
pairs: Low-flow oxygen with easy speaking and eating
Requires minimum flow to prevent CO₂ rebreathing
matchOptions: Low-flow oxygen with easy speaking and eating
Requires minimum flow to prevent CO₂ rebreathing

legacyQuestion.stem: A patient reports receiving Reiki sessions. Which category does the course associate with Reiki?
legacyQuestion.why: The lecture groups Reiki and healing touch with bioenergetic approaches.

legacyQuestion.stem: An older adult with dementia grimaces and guards the abdomen during repositioning. Which approach is appropriate?
legacyQuestion.why: Behavioral cues help assess pain when self-report is limited.
options: Assume no pain because the patient cannot rate it
Use a validated behavioral pain assessment and assess possible causes
Ask only the roommate about pain

legacyQuestion.stem: A family member lights a candle in the room of a patient receiving oxygen. What should the nurse do first?
legacyQuestion.why: Oxygen supports combustion; flames are unsafe around oxygen equipment.
options: Remove the ignition source and reinforce oxygen fire safety
Lower oxygen until the candle burns out
Ignore it if the oxygen is via nasal cannula

legacyQuestion.stem: A client reports a dull ache in the right shoulder after a meal. The provider suspects gallbladder disease. Which explanation best accounts for the shoulder discomfort?
legacyQuestion.why: Visceral pain can be perceived at a location distant from the involved organ.
options: Referred pain from a visceral source

legacyQuestion.stem: A COPD patient reports thicker sputum, worsening cough, and greater dyspnea than usual. What should the nurse do?
legacyQuestion.why: Changes from baseline may indicate COPD exacerbation requiring evaluation.
options: Assess for an exacerbation and report changes promptly
Assume the findings are expected and ignore them

legacyQuestion.stem: The nurse is setting up a Venturi mask. Which action is essential for ordered oxygen concentration?
legacyQuestion.why: Venturi devices require the correct adapter and flow to deliver the selected FiO₂.
options: Use the correct adapter and prescribed flow settings
Use any flow rate without checking the device

legacyQuestion.stem: A patient on nasal oxygen develops dry nasal mucosa. Which response is appropriate?
legacyQuestion.why: Assess oxygen-related dryness and use oxygen-safe measures.
options: Check the oxygen equipment and prescribed settings
Apply petroleum jelly inside the nostrils

legacyQuestion.stem: Which actions are consistent with tornado precautions? Select all that apply.
legacyQuestion.why: Shelter in protected areas and follow facility guidance.
options: Move ambulatory patients toward designated protected interior areas
Use elevators routinely regardless of conditions

legacyQuestion.stem: A patient with COPD exhales through pursed lips. What is the intended benefit?
legacyQuestion.why: Pursed-lip breathing helps maintain airway pressure during exhalation.
options: Prolong exhalation and help reduce air trapping
Eliminate the need for all prescribed therapy
Stop air from leaving the lungs

legacyQuestion.stem: A patient asks the nurse to demonstrate pursed-lip breathing. Which instruction is correct?
legacyQuestion.why: The technique uses a slow, prolonged exhalation through pursed lips.
options: Inhale gently through the nose and exhale slowly through pursed lips
Inhale and exhale rapidly through the mouth
Hold the breath for as long as possible
Exhale forcefully with an open mouth

legacyQuestion.stem: Match each communication or sensory condition to its defining characteristic.
legacyQuestion.why: Communication and sensory concepts are distinguished by the primary deficit.

legacyQuestion.stem: A patient declines to disclose an herbal supplement after feeling judged. Which response best restores therapeutic communication?
legacyQuestion.why: Nonjudgmental inquiry supports a complete care history.
options: “I ask everyone because supplements can affect treatment; what do you take?”

legacyQuestion.stem: An IM order is 30 mg. A vial contains 50 mg/mL. How many mL should the nurse draw up?
A patient with COPD asks why stopping smoking matters despite established lung disease. What should the nurse emphasize?
legacyQuestion.why: Smoking cessation remains important for COPD.
options: Avoiding smoke can reduce further lung injury
Stopping has no benefit with established COPD
Smoking is safe near oxygen if the flow is low

legacyQuestion.stem: Which question is most likely to elicit an accurate complementary-therapy history?
legacyQuestion.why: Open, nonjudgmental questioning encourages disclosure.
options: “You don't take any unapproved remedies, do you?”
“What vitamins, supplements, herbs, or other therapies do you use?”

legacyQuestion.stem: A patient has lower-back pain that travels down one leg. Which assessment detail is most important to clarify the pattern?
legacyQuestion.why: Location and radiation help characterize pain and guide follow-up.
options: Whether pain radiates and where it travels

legacyQuestion.stem: A patient asks whether acupuncture should replace prescribed treatment for an acute infection. Which response is safest?
legacyQuestion.why: Complementary therapies should not automatically displace indicated medical treatment.
options: “Let's discuss complementary options with the team without stopping prescribed treatment.”
“There is no reason to tell the provider.”

legacyQuestion.stem: A patient with expressive aphasia points to a body diagram but cannot name the painful area. What should the nurse do?
legacyQuestion.why: Alternative communication methods support assessment when speech is impaired.
options: Use the picture board and yes/no questions to clarify needs

legacyQuestion.stem: An older adult becomes dizzy when standing and has fallen twice recently. Which interventions reduce fall risk? Select all that apply.
legacyQuestion.why: Environmental precautions and appropriate assistance reduce fall risk.
options: Keep the bed low and locked
Place the call light within reach

legacyQuestion.stem: A hospitalized patient with intact hearing and vision has spent days alone with little conversation and reports feeling disconnected. Which problem is most likely?
legacyQuestion.why: Insufficient meaningful stimulation can cause sensory deprivation even with intact senses.
